page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it utilizes an Intel processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for accelerated vector and matrix operations, alongside cryptographic standards like AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile characterized by average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core and memory throughput. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core CPU test (1561.99) and Geekbench single-core score (1807.0), fall within the average range. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression (28.23 GB/sec) and static web serving throughput (6.53 GB/sec) demonstrate moderate performance. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks are positioned in the lower tier. The Geekbench multi-core score (4100.0) and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance (3213.05) are weak, as are the memory bandwidth metrics, with uncached read speeds at 32.36 GB/sec and write speeds at 21.01 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-4 offers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, representing a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-threaded processing. Given its performance profile, this instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded data processing, basic text processing, and small-scale application hosting. It is less optimal for memory-bound databases, software compilation, or multi-threaded high-performance computing tasks due to the observed bottlenecks in multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth.

The instance does not include local storage or GPUs.
